# American Time Use Survey (ATUS): agent index

BLS's survey of how Americans aged 15 and over spend their time, from a 24-hour time diary, conducted by the Census Bureau since 2003 with households leaving the Current Population Survey.

Publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). Dataset id: `atus`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the year.

## Releases

| Release | Table | Variables | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2003-2025` | respondent | 15 | ATUS 2003-2025 multi-year microdata files |
| `2003-2025` | summary | 456 | ATUS 2003-2025 multi-year microdata files |
| `2003-2025` | activity | 9 | ATUS 2003-2025 multi-year microdata files |
| `2003-2025` | replicates | 161 | ATUS 2003-2025 multi-year microdata files |

Tables in `2003-2025`: the key identifies a row; a reference says which columns join to another table, and when.

- `respondent`: Respondent file: one record per respondent. Key: TUCASEID
- `summary`: Activity summary file: one record per respondent, with minutes on each activity code. Key: TUCASEID. References: TUCASEID -> respondent
- `activity`: Activity file: one record per activity in the diary. Key: TUCASEID, TUACTIVITY_N. References: TUCASEID -> respondent
- `replicates`: Replicate weights file: 160 replicates of TUFNWGTP per respondent. Key: TUCASEID. References: TUCASEID -> respondent

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves by form | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span. `1972-1985,1987-2024 (not 1986)` means the release has a 1986 wave and the variable wasn't in it. `all 1972-1987; form A,C 1988-2024` means everyone was asked through 1987 and only forms A and C from 1988. The release's waves are: `2003-2025`: 2003-2025. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

`SKILL.md` says how to label an answer drawn from these files.
